acceptance_criteria.criterion: '{if begins-with: $VAR "pre"}' translates to '{% if var is string_startingwith "pre" %}'
Case-insensitive begins-with applies '|lower' to variable and lowercases the term
'{if ends-with: $VAR "suffix"}' translates to '{% if var[-6:] == "suffix" %}' (N = mb_strlen of term)
Case-insensitive ends-with applies '|lower' to slice expression and lowercases the term
Both {if} and {elseif} variants produce correct output via shared AbstractIfBase

comments.note: All 6 AC confirmed via IfBeginsWithTests (test_beginsWith + test_endsWith). The ends-with case-insensitive produces var|lower[-N:] == term correctly. mb_strlen used for multi-byte safety. PHPStan: zero new violations in touched files.

Edge case: zero-length term string would pass mb_strlen(0) = 0 producing var[-0:] which in Jinja evaluates to the whole string — effectively always matches. Very unlikely in practice but worth noting.

summary: All six acceptance criteria are met.
Implementation correctly handles starts/ends modes, case-insensitive |lower path, and mb_strlen for multi-byte safety.
No blocking issues found. Three low-priority non-blocking observations recorded as comments.

comments.note: Signature carries Mailcode_Variables_Variable (required for formatVariableName()) and matches all call sites in IfTranslation.php and ElseIfTranslation.php exactly. The WP spec described a simplified form; the actual implementation is correct.

Minor inconsistency: _translateSearch uses strtolower() while _translateContains uses mb_strtolower(). Both are functionally correct for ASCII and most Latin inputs but mb_strtolower would be more consistent for multi-byte search terms. Non-blocking, worth aligning in a cleanup pass.

Zero-length search term: mb_strlen('') = 0, producing var[-0:] which in Jinja/HubL evaluates to the whole string (always matches). Vanishingly unlikely in practice as upstream validation guards this. Non-blocking; noted consistent with QA observation.

Test coverage: 7 assertions across test_beginsWith and test_endsWith cover all six ACs including the single-char edge case, case-insensitive variant, and ElseIf delegates. Pattern (HubLTestCase + runCommands) is correct and consistent with the rest of the translator test suite.
